entries.recommendedTitle: Two men go up to pray
entries.alt: Two men climb stone steps toward a temple entrance: one in a light hooded robe ahead, and a balding man in muted olive and brown behind him.
entries.caption: In Jesus' parable, two men go up to the temple to pray: a Pharisee and a publican. The shared destination introduces two very different prayers.
entries.findings: Corrected01-v2 clearly ascends: lead feet placed on higher treads and bodies oriented toward entrance. Both men's hands, sandals and stair contact are plausible. Distinct identities: hooded full-bearded dark-haired Pharisee; balding, curly-sided short-bearded publican in olive/brown. Natural expressions and photographic stone/cloth/skin. Original descending version rejected.
conditions: Only revised01-v2 hash passes; original descending image remains rejected.
Stairs, garments and temple surroundings are illustrative, not an exact architectural reconstruction or a rule identifying religious character from clothing.

entries.alt: The man in the light hooded robe stands with both palms raised and looks upward in the temple court.
entries.caption: The Pharisee thanks God that he is unlike other people, including the publican. He speaks of his fasting and tithing, placing his own record at the center of his prayer.
entries.findings: Same hooded face, dark full beard, light fringed striped robe as01-v2. Both palms and fingers coherent; upward prayer gaze appropriate, not a failure of interpersonal eye contact. Restrained expression avoids cartoon villainy. Photographic textures, no exaggerated anatomy.
conditions: Prayer's self-comparison is established by Luke18:11–12, not inferred merely from upward gaze or raised palms.
Do not generalize this fictional man's fault to all Pharisees or Jewish worshippers; no named historical portrait.

entries.alt: The balding man stands apart beside a column with his head bowed and one hand against his chest, while the light-robed man prays farther away.
entries.caption: Standing afar off, the publican will not lift his eyes to heaven and beats upon his breast. His prayer is a plea for God to be merciful to him, a sinner.
entries.findings: Publican's bald crown, dark side curls, short beard, olive tunic, rope belt and brown wrap match01-v2. Bowed head and hand-to-chest contact align with source; hanging hand coherent. Distant Pharisee continues02 posture and garment. Distance is clear; dignified remorse rather than humiliating caricature. Prayer-directed lowered gaze is explicitly appropriate.
conditions: Still shows chest contact, not measurable repeated striking; caption's action is sourced from Luke18:13.
No inferred crime, profession-specific misconduct or outcome outside the cited verse is asserted.
